Microsoft's newest release notes list build 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac, can point at the right menu while you work.

blocks.text: Most lawyers use Outlook for Mac for three jobs. They file client email, reuse the same letters, and keep a calendar full of hearings and calls. Each job has a weak spot. Filing is manual. Search covers the mailbox you are in. LexWorkplace, a vendor that sells a document management add-in, also says Outlook offers no audit trail for client communications. Those three gaps give you a clear list to work through.
Check which Outlook for Mac you are running

Look at the left edge of the window. If Mail, Calendar and People sit in a vertical bar, you are on the new layout. Microsoft says that bar appears automatically in Outlook for Mac 16.71.0 or later. To see your exact build, open Outlook > About Outlook. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114 from October 14, 2026, and the newest Outlook entry is 16.114.3, from October 27, 2026. That entry lists general quality fixes only.

If your window still shows the older ribbon, you may be on legacy Outlook. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops connecting to Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. Help > Check for Updates or the App Store can bring the new experience to an older install. Firms that run Exchange On-Premises get a longer runway, as covered later on this page.

blocks.title: Check the legacy date with IT
blocks.text: Microsoft's support page gives October 2026 for Exchange Online. That date has passed as of November 6, 2026. Confirm with your IT admin, because timing can differ by firm before you change anything.
Set up the toolbar and left rail for legal work

The new Outlook replaces the ribbon with a customizable toolbar. Click the more icon, then choose Customize Toolbar. Keep the buttons you use all day, such as Reply and Move, in front. Remove the rest. A short toolbar is faster to scan when the inbox fills up.

The left rail holds Mail, Calendar and People. Build 16.109, dated May 12, 2026, made that rail reorderable. Drag Calendar above Mail if your day runs on hearings and calls more than on inbox triage. Build 16.108, dated April 14, 2026, also redesigned Settings. Older guides may show different paths for the same setting.

For daily tasks, press Shift+Command+] to open My Day. It sits in the View menu as a task pane. Use it when partners send requests by email and you need one list to track them. Turn it off if it adds clutter to your window.
Build templates for letters you send every week

Templates save the most time for lawyers. Think of the follow-up after a first client call, the cover note for an engagement letter, a document request, and a hearing confirmation. Each one takes time to write from scratch. A saved template turns that work into a short edit and a send.

To make one, select the email, then choose File > Save As Template. To reuse it, choose File > New > Mail From Template and pick the saved template. Microsoft says this needs Microsoft 365 and Outlook for Mac 15.35, build 170610, or later. Check your build before you tell a colleague the feature is missing.

Start with a short set. Put placeholders in square brackets, such as [CLIENT NAME] and [HEARING DATE], so you can find each gap with a search before you send. Read the greeting, the signature and any attachment note every time. Those three spots are easy to miss on a fast send.

A second option is the My Templates add-in. Go to New Mail > My Templates > +Template to build one. Microsoft says it works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. If you do not see it, your organization may have turned off add-ins.

blocks.title: Test before you trust a template
blocks.text: Send each new template to yourself first. Open it on your phone. Check the names, the dates and the signature block. A template you have not tested is a risk, not a shortcut.
Keep client email filed to the right matter

Outlook does not file a client email to a matter on its own. LexWorkplace describes the usual habit: one folder per client or matter, with messages moved there by hand. It calls that a starting point, not a system. Folders are personal, so the record often sits in one person's mailbox.

Manual export creates its own problems. Saving a message to a shared drive as PDF, EML or MSG strips threading and metadata, according to LexWorkplace. A document management system add-in can add a button and a sidebar to save email to a matter. Ask your IT team whether your firm has one before you assume it does.

A simple habit beats a perfect system you never use. Write one rule for the team and keep it short. For example: any email that changes a matter's status goes into that matter's folder the same day. A short Friday check beats a month of rebuilding a thread.
Why speed matters for client email

Client responsiveness is a known weak point. In Clio's 2024 Legal Trends Report, as summarized by 2Civility, only 1 in 3 law firms (33%) responded to emails from secret shoppers. A fast, accurate reply is one thing you control in that gap. Speed is the easiest place to start.

The same Clio summary says automatable tasks, such as client intake and firm data analysis, often make up 66% of hourly billable work. It estimates 57% of lawyers' tasks are automatable, against 69% for paralegals and 81% for administrative assistants. Repeat email replies are one example of that kind of work. These figures do not measure how long email takes, so treat them as a reason to automate repeat steps, not as a time study.
Search your mail without losing the thread

Press Shift+Command+F to search. Microsoft says search is powered by Microsoft Search. Type a client name, a matter code or a phrase from the subject line. Then use the filters to narrow by sender or date. Search finds what is in the mailbox you can see, so scope matters as much as keywords.

Scope is the trap. LexWorkplace says search covers only the individual mailbox, not the firm. If a colleague copied you on the key thread, you may find it in their mailbox and not yours. Ask IT how search works for shared mailboxes at your firm before you rely on it near a deadline.

Subject lines help more than most people expect. Put a short matter code in every subject, such as HW-CONTRACT or a client tag. Ask colleagues to keep that tag in their replies. Then a search for the tag finds the whole thread, not just the first message.

blocks.text: Where Lazur fits into your Outlook work

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Walk through one client email, step by step

Say a client email is open, and you want it in the Hartwell folder. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say: walk me through moving this to the Hartwell folder. Lazur names the first click and waits. You make the click. Then it names the next one. Lazur does not move the email for you.

The same method works for other menus you rarely use. Ask where Save As Template is, and Lazur circles the File menu. Ask what a rule dialog means, and Lazur explains each condition out loud. You keep your hands on the mouse and learn the path at the same time.
Dictate replies and draft text without retyping

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Dictation is included with Lazur. Add case names, judge names and opposing firm names to the personal dictionary, so the text comes out right the first time. Snippets handle standard closing paragraphs. Clipboard slots keep reused text within reach.

Ask Lazur to draft when the words are the hard part. For example: draft a reply that confirms the hearing time and asks for the signed engagement letter. Lazur drafts and types the text where you are working. Read every line before you send. Check dates, names and any legal point against the file.
What Lazur does not do in Outlook

Lazur does not click buttons or operate Outlook for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It points, guides, explains, answers out loud, drafts and types text. It also runs everyday actions such as Apple Reminders and Calendar events.

Set the job clearly. Ask Lazur to explain a dialog, circle a button or draft a reply. Do not expect it to file, delete or send mail. Those actions stay with you. That split keeps a person in charge of every client message.
Client confidentiality and what Lazur sends

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. Lazur says those providers do not store them. Content is never used to train AI models.

blocks.title: Check firm policy first
blocks.text: A screen can show privileged material. Before you ask a question with client names in view, check your firm's policy on AI tools. Hide the file or the client name if the policy asks for it.
Mistakes that slow lawyers down in Outlook for Mac

items: Treating an email as filed because it sits in Outlook. LexWorkplace describes that as captured but never actually filed.
Expecting the My Templates add-in in a shared mailbox. Microsoft says it is not available there.
Exporting email as PDF to a shared drive and losing the thread. Threading and metadata go with it.
Staying on legacy Outlook past the Exchange Online date. Connections stop from October 2026 on Microsoft's timeline.
Skipping the Outbox check. Since build 16.111 you can edit a message in the Outbox before it sends.
Searching from memory of a subject line. Use a matter code in the subject so search finds the thread later.

blocks.text: Rules, signatures and imports after the 2026 updates

Rules and signatures sit in Settings. Build 16.108 redesigned Settings, so the path may differ from older guides. Look through Settings for Rules or Signature. Test a rule on one message before you turn it on for the whole inbox. A bad rule can move mail you need.

Import PST arrived in build 16.110, dated June 16, 2026. Build 16.108 also added opening and importing .msg files. If you bring in an old archive, import it into a test folder first. Check one matter's thread, then move the rest.

Build 16.111, dated July 14, 2026, lets you edit a message in the Outbox before it sends. Open the Outbox and check any message queued for later. That check catches wrong attachments and wrong client names before they leave.
Legacy Outlook deadline and the steps to take

items: Open Outlook > About Outlook and note your build.
Ask your IT admin whether your firm's Exchange Online accounts still use legacy Outlook.
If you are on legacy, use Help > Check for Updates or the App Store to reach the new experience.
Use Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook only after you confirm it still connects for your account.
Keep a list of your templates, rules and signatures somewhere safe before you switch.

blocks.text: Microsoft says the EWS service is retired on October 1, 2026. Any tool that depends on EWS may stop working on that date. Ask IT whether any of your tools rely on it.

Firms on Exchange On-Premises have more time. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac keeps working with those mailboxes until October 9, 2029, and it gets only security updates until then. Confirm which group your firm is in before you plan the switch.
A plan for the week of setup

items: Monday: check your build, the left rail and the toolbar.
Tuesday: write templates for the letters you send most.
Wednesday: agree one filing rule with your team and write it down.
Thursday: test search on one live matter and note what you miss.
Friday: run a short filing check and fix the gaps you found.
Any day: ask Lazur to walk you through the menu you still hunt for.

blocks.text: Where Outlook ends and Word begins

Outlook holds the email. Word holds the draft, the clause and the redline. If the real work sits in an attachment, open it in Word and use Track Changes and Compare there. See [Microsoft Word for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers/word) for that side of the job. For the wider legal workflow, see [AI assistant for lawyers on Mac](/for/lawyers).
Next steps

Get Lazur from the [download page](/download) when you are ready. Check [plans on the pricing page](/pricing) before you start, since the trial begins when you first open the app. For screen-by-screen help in Outlook, see [Outlook on Mac with Lazur](/apps/outlook).

faq.question: Which version of Outlook for Mac should lawyers use in 2026?
faq.answer: Use the new Outlook for Mac. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114 from October 14, 2026, and 16.114.3 from October 27, 2026. Legacy Outlook for Mac stops connecting to Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. Check your build under Outlook > About Outlook.

faq.question: Does Outlook for Mac file client emails to a matter for me?
faq.answer: No. Most firms file by hand into a folder for each client or matter. LexWorkplace says Outlook offers no audit trail for client communications. A document management add-in can save email to a matter if your firm has one.

faq.question: Can I use templates in a shared mailbox?
faq.answer: The My Templates add-in is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. The File > Save As Template route needs Microsoft 365 and Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later. Ask IT to confirm which route works for your shared mailbox.

faq.question: Why can't I see the My Templates add-in?
faq.answer: Microsoft says it works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. If it is missing, your organization may have turned off add-ins. Ask your IT team before you change any settings.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or send email in Outlook for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, guides you one click at a time, explains screens, and drafts or types text. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You make each click and send each message.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my screen or audio to a server?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and Lazur says they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your firm's AI policy before you use it near privileged files.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook or any other app, and it has no partnership with any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: What is the legacy Outlook deadline for lawyers?
faq.answer: Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops connecting to Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. Exchange On-Premises mailboxes keep working until October 9, 2029, with security updates only. Confirm the timing for your firm with your IT admin.
